title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
sponsor_context: Formal sponsor of S. 1071, the originating legislative vehicle; the NDAA text was substituted later in the process.
last_action: Enacted as the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026.
summary: The FY2026 NDAA established new defense and intelligence safeguards for national-security AI research, biological data, model and supply-chain security, testing and oversight, frontier-AI planning, and intelligence-community use of public models.

substance_sections.title: National Security and Defense AI Institute
substance_sections.summary: Establishes a collaborative institute to support national-security and defense AI research, education, workforce development, testing, and transition into operational use.

substance_sections.title: Biological data for AI
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Defense Department to improve the security, availability, and responsible use of biological data for AI while addressing biotechnology, adversary-access, and national-security risks.

substance_sections.title: Defense-wide AI and machine-learning security
substance_sections.summary: Requires a department-wide cybersecurity and governance policy covering AI-specific attacks, supply-chain risk, life-cycle security, testing, auditing, monitoring, training, and incident response.

substance_sections.title: Security requirements for AI procurement
substance_sections.summary: Requires risk-based physical, cyber, workforce, supply-chain, monitoring, and incident-reporting standards for AI systems procured by the Defense Department.

substance_sections.title: Collaborative cybersecurity education
substance_sections.summary: Creates Defense Department partnerships with academic institutions to strengthen cybersecurity curricula, competencies, workforce pathways, and federal coordination; it supports the workforce needed to secure AI systems but is not itself AI-specific.

substance_sections.title: AI considerations in cybersecurity training
substance_sections.summary: Requires mandatory Defense Department cybersecurity training to cover the distinctive cybersecurity challenges created by AI use.

substance_sections.title: AI model assessment and oversight
substance_sections.summary: Creates a cross-functional team to establish a standardized framework and governance structure for evaluating and enabling Defense Department AI models.

substance_sections.title: AI sandbox environments
substance_sections.summary: Creates a task force to build secure environments for AI experimentation, training, familiarization, model evaluation, and responsible deployment across the Defense Department.

substance_sections.title: AI Futures Steering Committee
substance_sections.summary: Establishes a senior Defense Department committee to plan for advanced and frontier AI capabilities, examine risks and governance, and address safeguards including meaningful human control and override.

substance_sections.title: NSA AI security guidance
substance_sections.summary: Directs the NSA Artificial Intelligence Security Center to issue guidance protecting advanced AI and its supply chain from nation-state theft, sabotage, and compromise.

substance_sections.title: Intelligence-community AI development and use
substance_sections.summary: Strengthens intelligence-community AI leadership, coordination, reuse, acquisition terms, and tracking of model performance, safety, fairness, transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness.

substance_sections.title: Public AI models in classified environments
substance_sections.summary: Applies intelligence-community AI policies to public models hosted in classified systems and requires risk-based testing, benchmarks, and secure evaluation environments.

substance_sections.title: DeepSeek prohibition
substance_sections.summary: Bars DeepSeek from intelligence-community systems, subject to limited exceptions and required security mitigations.

committee_dynamics: These provisions were enacted across the defense and intelligence divisions of the FY2026 NDAA. S. 1071 originally addressed postal-service matters; the NDAA text was later substituted into that vehicle, so John Cornyn is the formal originating-bill sponsor rather than the NDAA's principal author.
advance_rationale: Enacted law; implementation replaces advancement forecasting.

responsible_agencies: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

deadlines.requirement: Establish the Artificial Intelligence Futures Steering Committee.
Establish the Defense Department AI sandbox task force under § 1534.
Establish the cross-functional AI model assessment team under § 1533.
Develop the Defense-wide AI and machine-learning cybersecurity policy and provide the implementation update for AI physical and cybersecurity procurement requirements.
Provide the AI sandbox task force briefing to the congressional defense committees under § 1534.
Submit the Defense Department review of AI and machine-learning cybersecurity and governance practices.
Identify commonly used intelligence-community AI systems and functions suitable for reuse.
Submit the AI Futures Steering Committee report to the congressional defense committees. The unclassified portion must also be made public.
Develop the standardized AI model assessment framework under § 1533.
